# core

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/core`.

## `sdk/core/device.js`

Which backend and which file variant a model runs with. The registry lists the variants of each model per backend in order of preference; this module never switches backend on its own: asking for a backend the model does not declare, or for WebGPU without a usable adapter, is an error.

### Type `WebGPUProbe`

```ts
{ available: boolean, shaderF16: boolean, fallbackAdapter: boolean, reason?: string }
```

### Type `DeviceRequest`

```ts
'auto'|'webgpu'|'wasm'
```

### Type `DeviceChoice`

```ts
{ device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', dtype: string, variant: import('./registry.js').RegistryVariant, index: number }
```

### `probeWebGPU({ gpu, force = false } = {})`

Ask for a WebGPU adapter once per page or Worker. Only a real adapter counts:
a software fallback adapter is reported as unavailable.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `[opts]` | `{ gpu?: any, force?: boolean }` | `gpu` replaces navigator.gpu (tests) |

Returns `Promise<WebGPUProbe>`.

### `variantFits(variant, probe)`

True when a variant's condition holds for this probe.

### `chooseVariant(model, requested, probe)`

Pick the backend and the variant of a model.
`auto` takes WebGPU when the model declares it and there is a usable adapter,
else WebAssembly. An explicit backend is taken or refused, never swapped.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `import('./registry.js').RegistryModel` |  |
| `requested` | `DeviceRequest` |  |
| `probe` | `WebGPUProbe` |  |

Returns `DeviceChoice`.

### `ortVariantFor(models)`

The backends a site needs to ship for a set of models (decides the ONNX Runtime variant).

### `isShaderError(err)`

True when an error looks like a WebGPU shader or kernel failure. A site that
ran with device 'auto' on WebGPU retries once on WebAssembly after any failure;
this only labels the reason it reports.

### `threadCount({ isolated = Boolean(globalThis.crossOriginIsolated), cores = globalThis.navigator?.hardwareConcurrency || 1 } = {})`

Threads for ONNX Runtime's WebAssembly backend: one unless the page is
cross-origin isolated (the threaded build needs SharedArrayBuffer).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `[env]` | `{ isolated?: boolean, cores?: number }` |  |

## `sdk/core/errors.js`

One error type for the whole SDK, with a stable code set where the error is born. Same shape as the engine's EngineError: `code`, `cause`, `details`; the message is the human sentence, in English.

### `ERROR_CODES`

Every code an AiError can carry.
- store-unavailable: the model store iframe did not load, did not say it is ready, or did not answer the first question
- store-permission: the model store refused the request (this site may not ask for it)
- store-quota: the browser storage of the model store is full
- store-network: the download was cut; asking again resumes it
- integrity: a file does not have the size or the hash the registry pins
- not-in-registry: a model, repo, revision or file that the registry does not list
- device-unsupported: the model does not declare the requested backend
- webgpu-unavailable: WebGPU was requested and there is no usable adapter
- runtime-mismatch: a runtime loaded at a version other than the pinned one
- model-mismatch: the model is not what the registry describes (outputs, dictionary)
- aborted: cancelled through an AbortSignal
- decode-failed: an input could not be decoded
- unsupported-format: an input of a type the task does not take
- too-large: an input too large even after scaling it down
- out-of-memory: the runtime could not get the memory the model needs in this browser
- run-failed: anything else while running, with the original error as `cause`
- disposed: the task instance was disposed

### Type `AiErrorCode`

```ts
'store-unavailable'|'store-permission'|'store-quota'|'store-network'|'integrity'|'not-in-registry'| 'device-unsupported'|'webgpu-unavailable'|'runtime-mismatch'|'model-mismatch'|'aborted'|'decode-failed'| 'unsupported-format'|'too-large'|'out-of-memory'|'run-failed'|'disposed'
```

### `INPUT_ERROR_CODES`

Codes of errors about the input itself, raised before the model runs: the runtime is intact.

### `isOutOfMemory(err)`

True when an error says that memory could not be had: a C++ allocation that
failed inside the WebAssembly runtime (std::bad_alloc), a WebAssembly memory
that could not grow, or a buffer the browser would not allocate.

### `class AiError`

Error of the SDK. `code` is one of ERROR_CODES.

- `.constructor(code, message, { cause, details } = {})`

### `isAiError(err, code)`

True when `err` is an AiError (optionally with this code).

### `fromStoreError(msg, details)`

Turn an error answer of the model store into an AiError.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `msg` | `{ tipo?: string, message?: string }` |  |
| `[details]` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  |

### `toAiError(err, fallback = 'run-failed')`

Wrap anything thrown into an AiError, keeping AiErrors and aborts as they are.

### `serializeError(err)`

A plain object that survives postMessage.

### `deserializeError(obj)`

Rebuild an AiError from serializeError's output.

### `abortError(signal)`

An AiError('aborted') for a signal, or null when the signal is not aborted.

### `throwIfAborted(signal)`

Throw AiError('aborted') if the signal is aborted.

## `sdk/core/hub-url.js`

Hugging Face URLs. This is the only module of the repo that spells the Hub's host or its resolve path: everything else asks here.
 A pinned URL is https://huggingface.co/<owner>/<repo>/resolve/<40-hex commit>/<path>. Every path segment must start with a letter, digit, `_` or `-` and contain only those and dots: no `..`, no percent-escapes, no backslashes. URLs are normalised when fetched, so `…/resolve/<sha>/../../../other/repo/resolve/<branch>/x` would end up in another repository; the model store refuses those and so does this module.

### `HUB_ORIGIN`

Origin of the Hugging Face Hub.

### `PINNED_URL_RE`

A URL of a file pinned to a commit, as the model store accepts it. Groups: repo, revision, path.

### `isRepoId(repo)`

True when `repo` looks like `owner/name` with safe characters.

### `isSafePath(path)`

True when `path` is a relative path whose segments are all safe.

### `isCommit(revision)`

True when `revision` is a full 40-hex commit.

### `pinnedUrl(repo, revision, path)`

The pinned URL of one file.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `string` | `owner/name` |
| `revision` | `string` | 40-hex commit |
| `path` | `string` | path inside the repository |

### `parsePinnedUrl(url)`

Split a pinned URL.

Returns `{ repo: string, revision: string, path: string } \| null`.

### `parseResolveUrl(url)`

Split any resolve URL of the Hub (revision may be a branch name, as the ones
Transformers.js builds for `main`). Unsafe paths, queries and fragments give null.

Returns `{ repo: string, revision: string, path: string } \| null`.

### `isHubUrl(url)`

True for any URL on the Hub's origin (used to refuse what is not pinned).

### `storeKey(url)`

The key the model store gives a URL: the URL without query or fragment, with
every run of other characters turned into `_`, keeping the last 180.

### `repoPage(repo, revision)`

Link to the page of a repository on the Hub, at a revision.

## `sdk/core/image-input.js`

Images in and out of a task. On the page, anything image-like becomes what a Worker can receive without copying (Blob, ImageBitmap, ImageData). In the Worker, a Blob is sniffed by its first bytes (never by its name), decoded with its EXIF orientation applied, and scaled down when it is too large.
 Browsers decode a file at its full size even when asked for a smaller bitmap (createImageBitmap's resize options scale after decoding), so the size is read from the file's header first and a file of more than MAX_INPUT_PIXELS is refused with too-large before anything is decoded. A small file can declare a huge picture (a PNG of one colour compresses to almost nothing).

### `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS`

The most pixels an input may have (8192 × 8192). It covers the photos of
today's cameras; above it, a single decode would take more memory than a page
should, so the file is refused (too-large) before it is decoded.

### `sniffImageType(head)`

Image types the tasks decode, by their first bytes.

### `DECODABLE`

Types the browser decodes for the tasks. HEIC and TIFF are refused on purpose.

### `imageSize(head)`

Width and height of an image from the first bytes of its file, without
decoding it (the size as stored: an EXIF rotation swaps them but does not
change the number of pixels). Null when the header does not say, or is cut.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `head` | `Uint8Array\|ArrayBuffer` | the start of the file (the first megabyte is plenty) |

Returns `{ width: number, height: number } \| null`.

### `checkPixelBudget(blob, maxPixels = MAX_INPUT_PIXELS)`

Refuse an image file whose picture has more than `maxPixels` pixels, from its
header, before anything decodes it. Files whose header does not say are left
to the decoder (and checked again after it).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `blob` | `Blob` |  |
| `[maxPixels]` | `number` |  |

Returns `Promise<{ width: number, height: number } \| null>`: the size the header gives

### `previewBitmap(blob, { maxSide = 2048, maxPixels = MAX_INPUT_PIXELS } = {})`

On the page: a small copy of an image file to show, at most `maxSide` on its
longest side, with its EXIF orientation applied. The full-size decode it needs
is released at once, and a file over the pixel budget is refused first
(too-large), so showing a photo never keeps a full-size copy alive.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `blob` | `Blob` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ maxSide?: number, maxPixels?: number }` |  |

Returns `Promise<ImageBitmap>`.

### `toTransferable(input)`

On the page: turn an image-like input into something a Worker takes without
copying. Returns the value and the list of objects to transfer.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `Blob\|ImageBitmap\|ImageData\|HTMLImageElement\|HTMLCanvasElement\|OffscreenCanvas\|HTMLVideoElement\|VideoFrame` |  |

Returns `Promise<{ value: Blob\|ImageBitmap\|ImageData, transfer: Transferable[] }>`.

### `decodeImage(input, { maxSide = 0, close = true, maxPixels = MAX_INPUT_PIXELS } = {})`

In the Worker (or the page): decode an input to RGBA pixels.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `Blob\|ImageBitmap\|ImageData` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ maxSide?: number, close?: boolean, maxPixels?: number }` | `maxSide` scales the longest side down to it; a file whose picture has more than `maxPixels` pixels is refused (too-large) before decoding |

Returns `Promise<{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8ClampedArray, scaled: boolean, sourceWidth: number, sourceHeight: number }>`.

### `encodePng({ width, height, data })`

Encode RGBA pixels as PNG (needs OffscreenCanvas, so a browser realm).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `img` | `{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8ClampedArray }` |  |

Returns `Promise<Blob>`.

## `sdk/core/integrity.js`

The model store checks a file's size; this checks its content, the same two ways the store's `put` does: SHA-256 for LFS files and the git blob SHA-1 for the small ones, both pinned in the registry. Once a file passes in a browser, a note in this site's IndexedDB (`verified:<pinned url>:<size>`) saves the next check; with the note gone, it is checked again.

### `sha256Hex(bytes)`

SHA-256 of bytes, as hex.

### `gitBlobSha1(bytes)`

git blob SHA-1 of bytes (`blob <size>\0` + bytes), as hex.

### `createVerifiedMemo({ dbName = 'elffuss-ai', indexedDB: idb = globalThis.indexedDB } = {})`

A memo of verified files. IndexedDB when there is one, else memory.

Returns `{ has(key: string): Promise<boolean>, set(key: string): Promise<void> }`.

### `verifyFile(blob, meta, url, memo)`

Check one file against its registry entry.
Returns the bytes when it had to read them (so the caller does not read twice),
or null when a previous check in this browser already covers it.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `blob` | `Blob` |  |
| `meta` | `{ size: number, sha256?: string, gitOid?: string }` |  |
| `url` | `string` | the pinned URL (part of the memo key) |
| `memo` | `ReturnType<typeof createVerifiedMemo>` |  |

Returns `Promise<ArrayBuffer \| null>`.

## `sdk/core/progress.js`

Progress of a load, in bytes, computed from the registry's sizes and the model store's progress messages (never from the runtime's own callbacks, which would trigger extra metadata requests).
 Every event is { status, loaded?, total?, file?, fromStore? } with status one of checking · downloading · loading · ready · running · done.

## `sdk/core/queue.js`

A queue of turns. ONNX Runtime Web cannot run two sessions of one instance at the same time on WebGPU ("Session already started"), and Transformers.js keeps its own chains that break after a failure, so every run of a task goes through one of these. A rejected turn does not stop the next one.

### `createQueue()`

Returns `{ run<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>, readonly pending: number, idle(): Promise<void> }`.

## `sdk/core/store-client.js`

Client of the shared model store of the Elffuss sites: a hidden iframe of https://models.elffuss.com/ that keeps model files in its own origin's storage and downloads what it does not have from the pinned Hugging Face URL. The page never talks to Hugging Face itself, so its CSP keeps connect-src 'self'.
 The tools only ask three things: whether a file is there (`has`), the file (`get`, always with its exact size) and to stop a download (`cancel`). They never empty the store, never save copies into it and never list it.
 Needs a document (the iframe); a Worker reaches it through store-bridge.js.

### `DEFAULT_STORE_URL`

The model store of the Elffuss sites.

### Type `StoreProgress`

```ts
{ loaded: number, total: number, resumedFrom?: number, retry?: number, waiting?: boolean }
```

### Type `StoreClient`

```ts
{ readonly origin: string, ready(): Promise<{ version: number, can: string[] }>, has(url: string, bytes: number): Promise<boolean>, get(url: string, opts: { bytes: number, signal?: AbortSignal, onProgress?: (p: StoreProgress) => void }): Promise<Blob>, cancel(url: string): void, pending(): string[], dispose(): void }
```

## `sdk/core/task-runtime.js`

What runs where the model runs (a Worker, or the page with worker: false): read the registry, pick the backend and variant, ask the store what it has, and hand the task's implementation a context with everything it may use.
 A task implementation (sdk/<task>/impl.js) exports: and never fetches, never touches the DOM and never reads files by itself.

### Type `LoadOptions`

```ts
{ model?: string, device?: import('./device.js').DeviceRequest, registry?: import('./registry.js').Registry, registryUrl?: string, runtime: import('./runtimes.js').RuntimeUrls, test?: TestFlags | null }
```

### Type `TestFlags`

```ts
{ pins?: Partial<typeof PINS>, failLoad?: boolean, failRun?: boolean }
```

Test builds only: `pins` replaces the expected runtime versions (to prove the check fails); `failLoad` asks impl.load to create a session from bytes that are not a model, and `failRun` asks impl.run to feed the model an input of an impossible shape, both inside the runtime. The Task passes each of them to the first load or run only.

### Type `LoadInfo`

```ts
{ model: string, task: string, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', dtype: string, fromStore: boolean, bytes: number, files: string[] }
```

### `class TaskContext`

What a task implementation may use. One per load.

- `.report(status, extra)`: Report a status of the run (`running`, `done`).
- `.transformers()`: Transformers.js, pinned and set up.
- `.pipeline()`: The Transformers.js pipeline of this model and variant, fed by the store.
- `.ort()`: ONNX Runtime Web, pinned and set up (direct use).
- `.bytes(ref)`: The bytes of one file of the variant, from the store, checked against the registry.
- `.text(ref)`: Text of one small file of the variant (UTF-8).
- `.session(ref, opts)`: An ONNX Runtime session of one file of the variant, on this load's backend.

## `sdk/core/task.js`

The base of every task class of the SDK (RemoveBg, Depth, Detect, Ocr): options, load once, runs in order, cancel, dispose, and where the model runs.

 With `worker: true` (the default in a browser) the model runs in a module Worker that is replaced after any failure; with `worker: false` it runs here, and a failure leaves the instance unusable (create another one).

### Type `TaskOptions`

```ts
{ device?: 'auto'|'webgpu'|'wasm', model?: string, onProgress?: (p: import('./progress.js').ProgressEvent) => void, signal?: AbortSignal, worker?: boolean, store?: import('./store-client.js').StoreClient, storeUrl?: string, runtime?: ReturnType<typeof runtimeUrls>, registryUrl?: string, registry?: import('./registry.js').Registry, onCspViolation?: (v: object) => void, test?: import('./task-runtime.js').TestFlags | null }
```

`store` is any object with has(url, bytes) and get(url, { bytes, signal, onProgress }); by default the Elffuss model store. `runtime` are the same-origin URLs of the runtimes (the site's build writes them).

### Type `TaskSpec`

```ts
{ task: string, workerUrl: URL, impl: () => Promise<any>, prepare?: (input: any) => Promise<{ value: any, transfer: Transferable[] }> }
```

### `class Task`

Base class of the task modules: one model, loaded once, runs one after another.
A task module passes its spec (task name, Worker URL, implementation) and the
caller's options.

- `.constructor(spec, options = {})`
- `.device`: Backend used, after load().
- `.dtype`: Variant dtype used, after load().
- `.info`: Everything load() returned, or null.
- `.load({ signal } = {})`: Download (through the store) and prepare the model. Idempotent; concurrent calls share one load.
- `.run(input, { signal, ...opts } = {})`: Run the task once. Loads first if needed; runs of one instance go one after another.
- `.dispose()`: Release the model and the Worker. Idempotent; waits for a run in progress.

### `oneShot(TaskClass)`

Make the one-call form of a task class: load, run, dispose.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `TaskClass` | `new (o?: TaskOptions) => Task` |  |

Returns `(input: any, options?: TaskOptions & Record<string, any>) => Promise<T>`.

### `TASK_OPTIONS`

Options that belong to the task instance; the rest go to run().

## `sdk/core/tf-env.js`

Transformers.js, set up once per Worker and only ever fed through the model store. Two facts of 4.3.1 shape this module: - pipeline() asks for config.json and probes preprocessor_config.json at the - session creation and runs are queued on two global promise chains that do

### `loadTransformers(runtime, { pins = PINS } = {})`

Import the pinned ONNX Runtime bundle and the Transformers.js copy that points
at it, set Transformers.js up, and check the versions. Once per realm.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | `{ ortBundle: string, ortMjs: string, ortWasm: string, transformers: string }` | same-origin URLs |
| `[opts]` | `{ pins?: typeof PINS }` | `pins` replaces the expected versions (test builds only) |

### `configureTransformers(env, { ortMjs, ortWasm, fetch = null })`

The settings every site uses. Nothing is cached in the site's own storage,
no blob: URLs are made for the runtime, and the network path is storeFetch.

### `createStoreFetch({ model, files, store, memo, progress, cached, baseFetch = globalThis.fetch?.bind(globalThis), log })`

The only way out for Transformers.js: a fetch that serves Hub URLs of this
model from the model store, at the pinned commit.
 - same origin: the normal fetch;
 - a Hub URL of a repo of this model, at the branch head or at the pinned commit:
     · a path the registry does not list for this variant → 404 (what the Hub would say)
     · a one-byte probe → a 206 made here with the registry's size
     · the whole file → the store, checked, as a 200;
 - anything else → not-in-registry.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `opts` | `{ model: import('./registry.js').RegistryModel, files: import('./registry.js').ResolvedFile[], store: { get(url: string, o: { bytes: number, onProgress?: Function }): Promise<Blob> }, memo: ReturnType<import('./integrity.js').createVerifiedMemo>, progress?: ReturnType<import('./progress.js').createProgress>, cached?: Map<string, boolean>, baseFetch?: typeof fetch, log?: (entry: object) => void }` |  |

### `createPipeline({ tf, model, choice, fetch })`

Create a Transformers.js pipeline for one model and variant, through the store.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `opts` | `{ tf: any, model: import('./registry.js').RegistryModel, choice: import('./device.js').DeviceChoice, fetch: (input: any, init?: any) => Promise<Response> }` |  |

## `sdk/core/tt.js`

The one Trusted Types policy of the sites, `elffuss-ai`. Their CSP requires Trusted Types for scripts, so a Worker can only be created from a URL this policy vouches for: same origin, under /v/ (a build) or /vendor/ (a runtime). Where the browser has no Trusted Types, the URL is checked the same way and passed on as a string.

### `SCRIPT_PREFIXES`

Paths a script URL may have.

### `isAllowedScriptUrl(url, origin = globalThis.location?.origin)`

True when `url` is a same-origin script under an allowed prefix.

### `scriptUrl(url)`

A script URL the CSP accepts for `new Worker()`.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string\|URL` |  |

Returns `TrustedScriptURL\|string`.

## `sdk/core/worker-host.js`

The page side of a task Worker. It creates the Worker through the Trusted Types policy, answers its store requests with the page's store client, and replaces it after any failure of the runtime: Transformers.js 4.3.1 keeps session creation and runs on global promise chains that stay broken after one rejection, so a Worker whose runtime failed is never reused. The files come back from the store, so a new Worker does not download anything again. A run refused for its input (a file that is not an image, or that cannot be decoded) never reached the runtime, so that Worker and its model are kept.
 Cancelling a call cancels the downloads it started (elffuss-model-cancel) and terminates the Worker, because ONNX Runtime cannot stop a run halfway.

### `createWorkerHost({ workerUrl, store, onCspViolation, readyTimeout = 30000, name = 'elffuss-ai-task' })`

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `opts` | `{ workerUrl: string\|URL, store: import('./store-client.js').StoreClient, onCspViolation?: (v: object) => void, readyTimeout?: number, name?: string }` |  |

## `sdk/core/worker-rpc.js`

The Worker side of a task. sdk/<task>/worker.js is two lines:

 Messages, page → Worker: { type: 'load', id, opts } · { type: 'run', id, input, opts } · { type: 'dispose', id } Worker → page: { type: 'ready' } once · { type: 'progress', id, progress } · { type: 'result', id, value } After an error the page replaces this Worker (see worker-host.js), so nothing here tries to recover a runtime that failed.

### `runResult(out)`

Normalise what impl.run returns: always `{ value, transfer }`.

### `serveTask(impl, { port = globalThis } = {})`

Serve one task implementation from this Worker.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `impl` | `{ task: string, load: Function, run: Function, dispose?: Function }` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ port?: any }` |  |

## `sdk/core/zip.js`

A small ZIP writer for exports (text only, built in memory): "store" method, UTF-8 names (general purpose bit 11), CRC-32 by table, central directory. No ZIP64, so at most 65,535 entries and 4 GiB. Names are sanitised: NFC, forward slashes, no leading slash, no `..` segments, no control characters, `<>:"|?*` replaced by `_`, and repeated names get " (2)", " (3)"…

### `crc32(bytes, crc = 0)`

CRC-32 (IEEE) of bytes, optionally continuing a previous value.

### `sanitizeZipPath(name)`

A safe relative path for a ZIP entry.

### `uniquePaths(names)`

Make every name unique by adding " (2)", " (3)"… before the extension.

### `createZip(entries, { date = new Date() } = {})`

Build a ZIP archive.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `entries` | `{ name: string, data: Uint8Array\|string }[]` |  |
| `[opts]` | `{ date?: Date }` | the modification time of every entry |

Returns `Uint8Array`.

### `readZip(bytes)`

Read back a ZIP written by createZip (store method only).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `bytes` | `Uint8Array` |  |

Returns `{ name: string, data: Uint8Array, crc: number, flags: number, method: number }[]`.
